title: Fallbacks and Graceful Degradation
summary: Providers go down, slow down and rate-limit you. This lesson turns that into numbers (availability, timeouts, hedged tails) and into design patterns: fallback providers, circuit breakers and degraded modes that keep a feature useful when the best path is gone.
objectives: Convert an availability percentage into minutes of downtime and combine serial dependencies
Compute the availability of a primary plus fallback, including the effect of correlated outages
Choose a timeout from a latency distribution and reason about retry amplification
Explain how hedged requests cut tail latency and what they cost
Design a circuit breaker and a ladder of degraded modes
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with probabilities of independent events, with percentiles such as p50 and p99 ([Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference)), and with the cost model from [Choosing and Routing Models](/learn/production-systems/model-routing). Retries and backoff were introduced for agents in [When Steps Fail](/learn/agents/failures-and-recovery).
